record.paper_title: Packings and coverings of groups: some results and open problems
record.context_brief: Packing spectrum of an infinite group
record.original_question: Let G be an infinite group. For a subset A of G, let pack(A) be the supremum of the cardinalities of families of pairwise disjoint left translates of A, and let Pack(G) be the set of all values pack(A) as A ranges over subsets of G. Is every infinite cardinal kappa with aleph_0 <= kappa <= |G| an element of Pack(G)?

evidence.quote: pack(A) = sup{|S|: S ⊆ G, {sA: s ∈ S} is disjoint},
Problem 1. Is it true that [ℵ0, G] ⊆ Pack(G) for every infinite group G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite group. For a subset $A\subseteq G$, define
\[ \operatorname{pack}(A) = \sup\{|S| : S\subseteq G \text{ and the family } \{sA : s\in S\} \text{ consists of pairwise disjoint sets}\}, \]
and let
\[ \operatorname{Pack}(G) = \{\operatorname{pack}(A) : A\subseteq G\}. \]
Determine whether, for every infinite group $G$, every cardinal $\kappa$ with $\aleph_0 \le \kappa \le |G|$ belongs to $\operatorname{Pack}(G)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for the packing-spectrum problem on infinite groups (Pack(G) as defined by Protasov) did not return a definitive resolution. Related literature on partitions, packings, and coverings of groups by Protasov and collaborators exists, but no source clearly confirming or refuting that every infinite cardinal κ with ℵ₀ ≤ κ ≤ |G| lies in Pack(G) was found.
